risk_review.notes: Independently reviewed the Definition, batch-14 def-two-level-full-factorial-design (empty product 1 and sign cube), the complete justified-by alias theorem, reader-15 and refute-15. Independent incidence rows have rank p, so every sign vector has 2^{k-p} solutions, including p=k. Generator multiplication is associative symmetric difference with sign multiplication; independent supports make all 2^p products distinct, and only the identity has empty support. Since p>=1 the finite nonidentity set is nonempty and its shortest positive length exists. Negative generators and k=p=1 are admitted; no arbitrary choice is used. The justified-by theorem proves existence and exact constant-word characterization without assuming them from this definition. NIST pri3342 tables 3.14-3.15, pri3343 signed-generator paragraphs, pri3344 defining-relation/resolution paragraphs and Oehlert section 18.2 printed pp.473-475 were read for the conventions. No defect or prerequisite blocker found.

citations.quote:
Fix integers $k\ge1$ and $1\le p\le k$, and put $[k]=\{1,\ldots,k\}$. Let $\mathbb F_2=\{0,1\}$ with addition and multiplication modulo $2$. For a factor subset $G\subseteq[k]$, its incidence vector $1_G\in\mathbb F_2^k$ has coordinate $1$ at $j$ exactly when $j\in G$. Choose $p$ subsets $G_1,\ldots,G_p$ whose incidence vectors are linearly independent over $\mathbb F_2$, and choose signs $s_i\in\{-1,+1\}$. Using the run space and product columns of [[def-two-level-full-factorial-design]], define the **regular fraction**

$$\mathcal F=\{x\in\{-1,+1\}^{[k]}:x_{G_i}=s_i\text{ for }1\le i\le p\},\qquad x_G=\prod_{j\in G}x_j.$$

The corresponding design is called a regular $2^{k-p}$ fractional factorial; [[thm-regular-fractional-factorial-aliasing-criterion]] proves that $\mathcal F$ has exactly $2^{k-p}$ runs, including the case $p=k$ with one run. The choices $s_i=-1$ are alternate fractions and are part of the definition.

A **signed word** is a pair $(\epsilon,A)$ with $\epsilon\in\{-1,+1\}$ and $A\subseteq[k]$. It evaluates at $x$ as $\epsilon x_A$ and multiplies by

$$(\epsilon,A)(\delta,B)=(\epsilon\delta,A\triangle B),\qquad A\triangle B=(A\setminus B)\cup(B\setminus A).$$

The identity word is $(+1,\varnothing)$. The signed generator $h_i=(s_i,G_i)$ evaluates to $+1$ on $\mathcal F$. The **defining subgroup** $H$ is generated by $h_1,\ldots,h_p$; the alias theorem proves it is exactly the subgroup of signed words that evaluate to $+1$ on every run in $\mathcal F$.

For $A,B\subseteq[k]$, their restricted sign columns are **equal-column aliases** when $x_A=x_B$ for every $x\in\mathcal F$. They are **signed aliases with sign $\sigma\in\{-1,+1\}$** when $x_A=\sigma x_B$ on every run; sign $+1$ is the equal-column case and sign $-1$ records opposite columns. The alias theorem gives the exact criterion for each sign.

The **word length** of $(\epsilon,A)$ is $|A|$, the number of factor letters, independent of $\epsilon$. The **resolution** is the minimum $|A|$ among nonidentity words $(\epsilon,A)\in H$; it is written as a Roman numeral. Since $p\ge1$ and the generators are independent, $H$ has a nonidentity word of nonzero length.

derivations.claim: Write each run coordinate as $x_j=(-1)^{z_j}$ and each generator sign as $s_i=(-1)^{b_i}$, with $z\in\mathbb F_2^k$ and $b\in\mathbb F_2^p$. Let $M$ have rows $1_{G_i}$. The equations for $\mathcal F$ become $Mz=b$. By [A1], $M$ has rank $p$; row reduction gives $p$ pivot coordinates and $k-p$ free coordinates, and every assignment of the free coordinates determines exactly one pivot assignment. Therefore $|\mathcal F|=2^{k-p}$.

Row-reduce $M$ to $R=UM$, where $U$ is invertible, and let $D=\{d_1,\ldots,d_p\}$ be the pivot coordinates; write $R_i$ for row $i$ of $R$. For a subset $C$, put $c=1_C$; on a solution $z$, $x_C=(-1)^{c\cdot z}$. Substitution of the pivot equations gives $c\cdot z=\sum_i c_{d_i}b'_i+\sum_{j\notin D}(c_j+\sum_i c_{d_i}R_{ij})z_j$, where $b'=Ub$. This exponent is constant over all free coordinates exactly when every displayed free-coordinate coefficient is zero. Since the pivot columns of $R$ are the identity, those equations say precisely that $c=\sum_i c_{d_i}R_i$, so $c$ lies in the row space of $M$.

If $c$ is outside the row space of $M$, step 2.1 shows that $x_C$ is nonconstant on $\mathcal F$, so neither sign $\epsilon$ makes $\epsilon x_C=+1$ on every run. If $c$ is in the row space, then $c=\sum_i\lambda_i1_{G_i}$ for a unique $\lambda\in\mathbb F_2^p$, and on $\mathcal F$ we have $x_C=(-1)^{\lambda\cdot b}=\prod_i s_i^{\lambda_i}$. Exactly one sign $\epsilon=\prod_i s_i^{\lambda_i}$ makes $\epsilon x_C=+1$ on all of the nonempty set $\mathcal F$, and $(\epsilon,C)=\prod_{i:\lambda_i=1}(s_i,G_i)$. Conversely, every such product evaluates to $+1$. Independence makes the $2^p$ choices of $\lambda$ distinct, proving that $H$ is precisely the set of constant-$+1$ signed words and $|H|=2^p$.

For any $A,B\subseteq[k]$, cancellation of repeated factors gives $x_Ax_B=x_{A\triangle B}$. Therefore $x_A=\sigma x_B$ on $\mathcal F$ exactly when $\sigma x_{A\triangle B}=+1$ there. By step 3.1 and the definition of $H$ in [F2], this is equivalent to $(\sigma,A\triangle B)\in H$. The case $\sigma=+1$ is equality of columns, and $\sigma=-1$ is opposition.

The empty support gives only (+1,empty); negative generator signs and one-run fractions satisfy the same argument. All operations are finite and use no AC. This is a proof-only repair; Statement, dependencies, citation quotes and page interfaces are unchanged. The finite F_2 argument is familiar and checked directly; no external source consultation is claimed for this adjudication.

derivations.claim: The two terms in the fitted vector combine as $\beta_Ac_A+\beta_Bc_B=\beta_A(\sigma c_B)+\beta_Bc_B=(\sigma\beta_A+\beta_B)c_B$. Thus the fitted vector depends on this pair only through $\sigma\beta_A+\beta_B$, with all other coefficients fixed.

For any $t\in\mathbb R$, replace $\beta_A$ by $\beta_A+t$ and $\beta_B$ by $\beta_B-\sigma t$. Then $\sigma(\beta_A+t)+(\beta_B-\sigma t)=\sigma\beta_A+\beta_B$, so the combination in step 1.1 and therefore $X\beta$ are unchanged. Because the error law is independent of $\beta$, the resulting response distributions are identical. Taking $t\ne0$ changes both coefficients, proving that neither is separately identifiable in the unrestricted model.

derivations.claim: For a signed word $(\epsilon,A)$ and an original run $x$, multiplication of its factors gives $\epsilon(\tau_Jx)_A=(-1)^{|A\cap J|}\epsilon x_A$. In particular, for $J=[k]$ the multiplier is $(-1)^{|A|}$.

Every word in $H$ evaluates to $+1$ on all original rows. By step 1.1 it evaluates to $(-1)^{|A\cap J|}$ on every appended row. Since both blocks are present, it is a constant-$+1$ relation on the stacked table exactly when $|A\cap J|$ is even. Any relation on the stacked table must also hold on its original rows and hence belong to $H$; therefore the residual subgroup is exactly $H_J$.

For any two effects, $x_A=\sigma x_B$ on a run table exactly when the signed word $(\sigma,A\triangle B)$ evaluates to $+1$ on every row. By step 2.1, an originally signed-aliased pair retains that relation on the stacked table precisely when $|(A\triangle B)\cap J|$ is even; if it is odd, the relation changes sign between blocks and no constant signed alias remains. A pair not signed-aliased on the original fraction cannot become one because the original rows remain in the augmented table. When $J=[k]$, $|A\triangle B|\equiv |A|+|B|\pmod2$, so exactly opposite-parity pairs separate among the original aliases, and even-word relations remain.

Proof steps 1.1–2.1 also cover J empty, with multiplier +1 and unchanged subgroup H. For J=[k], step 3.1 gives the full mirror and separation exactly of opposite-parity original aliases.

Statement: Step 2.1 proves that an odd-intersection relation changes sign on the appended rows and cannot be a constant signed alias.

derivations.claim: Choose $x_A,x_B\in\{-1,+1\}$ freely and set $x_C=x_Ax_B$. This gives exactly the four runs listed in the Example, one for each of the four choices of $(x_A,x_B)$, and every run satisfies $x_Ax_Bx_C=+1$.

Here $H=\{I,ABC\}$. By [F2], effects have equal columns exactly when their symmetric difference is either $\varnothing$ or $\{A,B,C\}$. Pairing each subset with its complement gives precisely $\{I,ABC\}$, $\{A,BC\}$, $\{B,AC\}$, and $\{C,AB\}$; these four pairs exhaust the eight subsets.

In each listed pair the columns are equal, so [F3] shows that the corresponding terms enter the fitted vector through $\beta_I+\beta_{ABC}$, $\beta_A+\beta_{BC}$, $\beta_B+\beta_{AC}$, or $\beta_C+\beta_{AB}$, respectively. The design by itself does not identify the two coefficients within any pair separately.

Then $|\mathcal F|=2^{k-p}$, $|H|=2^p$, and $H$ consists of all signed words $(\epsilon,C)$ for which $\epsilon x_C=+1$ on every run in $\mathcal F$. For all factor subsets $A,B\subseteq[k]$ and signs $\sigma\in\{-1,+1\}$,

$$x_A=\sigma x_B\text{ on }\mathcal F\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad(\sigma,A\triangle B)\in H.$$

In particular, the columns agree exactly when $(+1,A\triangle B)\in H$; a relation with sign $-1$ means the columns are opposites.

Let $\mathcal F$ be a regular fraction with signed defining subgroup $H$. For a specified set of factors $J\subseteq[k]$, define $\tau_Jx$ by $(\tau_Jx)_j=-x_j$ for $j\in J$ and $(\tau_Jx)_j=x_j$ for $j\notin J$. The **partial foldover** on $J$ is the run table formed by stacking the original runs with one transformed copy $\tau_J(\mathcal F)$; the **complete mirror foldover** is the case $J=[k]$. Its residual signed defining subgroup is exactly

$$H_J=\{(\epsilon,A)\in H:|A\cap J|\text{ is even}\}.$$

Thus an originally signed-aliased pair $A,B$ remains signed-aliased on the augmented table exactly when $|(A\triangle B)\cap J|$ is even; if it is odd, the pair is separated. For a complete mirror foldover, a word of order $r=|A\triangle B|$ changes sign by $(-1)^r$. Therefore aliases between effects of opposite order parity separate, while same-parity relations remain. The displayed formula gives the full residual alias set for every partial foldover; a selected-factor follow-up need not remove other aliases.

Let $c_A,c_B\in\mathbb R^{\mathcal F}$ be the columns for distinct factorial effects $A,B\subseteq[k]$ in a regular fraction, and suppose $c_A=\sigma c_B$ for a fixed $\sigma\in\{-1,+1\}$. Consider the unrestricted fixed-design linear model $Y=X\beta+\epsilon$, where these columns occur in $X$ and the distribution of the error vector $\epsilon$ does not depend on $\beta$. A coefficient combination is **identifiable** if it has the same value for all parameter vectors giving the same distribution of $Y$. The contribution of these two columns depends only on $\sigma\beta_A+\beta_B$; neither coefficient is separately identifiable while the parameter space remains unrestricted. For equal columns ($\sigma=+1$), the relevant combination is the sum; for opposite columns ($\sigma=-1$), it is the difference. Additional runs can remove the ambiguity only if they break the column relation, and hierarchy or sparsity restrictions are extra modeling assumptions.

derivations.claim: The equations give $x_Ax_Bx_D=+1$ and $x_Cx_Dx_E=+1$, so the defining words are $ABD$ and $CDE$. Their product is $ABCE$ because the repeated $D$ cancels in symmetric difference. The two incidence vectors are nonzero and distinct; over $\mathbb F_2$, two nonzero vectors are dependent only if equal, so these generators are independent. By [F2] these and the identity are exactly the four words in $H$. Their nonidentity lengths are $3,3,4$, hence the initial resolution is III.

For the complete mirror, [F3] changes the signs of the length-three relations ABD and CDE but preserves ABCE, giving $H_{[5]}=\{I,ABCE\}$. The two eight-run blocks are disjoint because ABD has opposite signs on them, and both lie in $Q=\{x:x_Ax_Bx_Cx_E=+1\}$; choosing $x_A,x_B,x_C,x_D$ freely determines $x_E$, so $|Q|=16$ and their union is exactly this regular $2^{5-1}$ fraction. Its aliases are precisely $S$ with $S\triangle\{A,B,C,E\}$, so $A$ remains paired with $BCE$, while $C\triangle DE=CDE$ is absent and that pair separates. The shortest residual word has length $4$.

For the partial foldover on $J=\{A\}$, [F3] changes ABD and ABCE but preserves CDE, giving $H_J=\{I,CDE\}$. The two eight-run blocks are disjoint because ABD has opposite signs on them, and both lie in $Q'=\{x:x_Cx_Dx_E=+1\}$; choosing $x_A,x_B,x_C,x_D$ freely determines $x_E$, so their union is all 16 runs in this regular $2^{5-1}$ fraction. The complete residual pairs are precisely $S$ and $S\triangle\{C,D,E\}$: this includes $C=DE$ and excludes the original relation $A=BD$. The shortest residual word has length $3$.

The retained columns $c_C=c_{DE}$ in the partial design contribute as $(\beta_C+\beta_{DE})c_C$. By [F4], only this combination enters the fitted vector for this pair, so the partial follow-up does not separately identify $\beta_C$ and $\beta_{DE}$ without a restriction or further runs.
